questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $f(x) = \begin{cases} x-2 & 0 \le x \le 2 \\ -2 & -2 \le x \le 0 \end{cases}$ and $h(x) = f(|x|) + |f(x)|$ then $\int_{0}^{k} h(x) \, dx$ is equal to ($k > 0$)
questions.solution:
$f(|x|) = \begin{cases} -2-x, & x < 0 \\ x-2, & x > 0 \end{cases}$
$|f(x)| = \begin{cases} 2, & x < 0 \\ 2-x, & x > 0 \end{cases}$
$\Rightarrow h(x) = f(|x|) + |f(x)| = \begin{cases} -x, & x < 0 \\ 0, & x > 0 \end{cases}$
$\Rightarrow \int_{0}^{k} h(x) \, dx = \int_{0}^{k} 0 \, dx = 0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Find the number of rational numbers in the expansion of $\left(2^{1/5} + 5^{1/3}\right)^{15}$.
questions.solution:
$T_{r+1} = {}^{15}\text{C}_r \left(2^{1/5}\right)^{15-r} \left(5^{1/3}\right)^r = {}^{15}\text{C}_r 2^{3-\frac{r}{5}} 5^{\frac{r}{3}}$
$r$ must be a multiple of both 5 and 3, so $r = 0, 15$.
So Total No. of Rational Terms is 2.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Find value of $\int_{0}^{\pi/2} \frac{\sin^2 x}{1 + \sin x \cos x} \, dx$
questions.solution:
$I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \frac{\cos^2 x}{1 + \sin x \cos x} \, dx$
$2I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \frac{1}{1 + \sin x \cos x} \, dx = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \frac{2 \, dx}{2 + \sin 2x} = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \frac{\sec^2 x \, dx}{\tan^2 x + \tan x + 1}$
Let $t = \tan x$, then $2I = \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{dt}{t^2 + t + 1} = \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{dt}{\left(t + \frac{1}{2}\right)^2 + \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \left[ \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2t+1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) \right]_0^{\infty}$
$2I = \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} \left[ \frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{\pi}{6} \right] \Rightarrow I = \frac{\pi}{3\sqrt{3}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $x^2 - ax + b = 0$ has roots 2, 6; and $\alpha = \frac{1}{2a+1}; \beta = \frac{1}{2b-a}$. Find equation having roots $\alpha, \beta$.
questions.solution:
$a = 2 + 6 = 8$
$b = 2 \times 6 = 12$
$\alpha = \frac{1}{17}, \beta = \frac{1}{16}$
Required EQ: $x^2 - (\alpha + \beta)x + \alpha\beta = 0 \Rightarrow x^2 - \left(\frac{1}{17} + \frac{1}{16}\right)x + \frac{1}{17} \times \frac{1}{16} = 0$
$\Rightarrow 272x^2 - 33x + 1 = 0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: 2, p and q are in G.P. In an A.P., 2 is third term, p is $7^{\text{th}}$ term and q is $8^{\text{th}}$ term. Find p and q.
questions.solution:
In G.P., $p = 2r, q = 2r^2$
In A.P.,
$A + 2d = 2$
$A + 6d = 2r$
$A + 7d = 2r^2$
By solving, $r = \frac{1}{4}$
$p = \frac{1}{2}, q = \frac{1}{8}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the domain of the function $\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{3x-22}{2x-19}\right) + \log_e\left(\frac{3x^2-8x+5}{x^2-3x-10}\right)$ is $[\alpha, \beta]$ then $3\alpha + 10\beta$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$-1 \le \frac{3x-22}{2x-19} \le 1 \Rightarrow \frac{3x-22}{2x-19} + 1 \ge 0 \Rightarrow \frac{5x-41}{2x-19} \ge 0 \Rightarrow x \in \left(-\infty, \frac{41}{5}\right] \cup \left(\frac{19}{2}, \infty\right)$
Also, $\frac{3x-22}{2x-19} - 1 \le 0 \Rightarrow \frac{x-3}{2x-19} \le 0 \Rightarrow x \in \left[3, \frac{19}{2}\right)$
Intersection gives $x \in \left[3, \frac{41}{5}\right]$.
For log domain, $\frac{(3x-5)(x-1)}{(x-5)(x+2)} > 0 \Rightarrow x \in (-\infty, -2) \cup \left(1, \frac{5}{3}\right) \cup (5, \infty)$
Intersection with $\left[3, \frac{41}{5}\right]$ gives $[\alpha, \beta] = \left[5, \frac{41}{5}\right]$.
$3\alpha + 10\beta = 3(5) + 10\left(\frac{41}{5}\right) = 15 + 82 = 97$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text:
$x + (2\sin 2\theta) y + 2\cos 2\theta = 0$
$x + (\sin\theta) y + \cos\theta = 0$
$x + (\cos\theta) y - \sin\theta = 0$
find nontrivial solution
questions.solution:
$\begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2\sin 2\theta & 2\cos 2\theta \\ 1 & \sin\theta & \cos\theta \\ 1 & \cos\theta & -\sin\theta \end{vmatrix} = 0$
$1[-\sin^2\theta - \cos^2\theta] - 2\sin 2\theta [-\sin\theta - \cos\theta] + 2\cos 2\theta [\cos\theta - \sin\theta] = 0$
$-1 + 2\sin 2\theta(\sin\theta + \cos\theta) + 2\cos 2\theta(\cos\theta - \sin\theta) = 0$
$-1 + 2\cos\theta + 2\sin\theta = 0 \Rightarrow \sin\theta + \cos\theta = \frac{1}{2}$
$\cos\left(\theta - \frac{\pi}{4}\right) = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}} = \cos\alpha \Rightarrow \alpha = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $f(x) = x^5 + 2e^{x/4}$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$. Consider a function $(g \circ f)(x) = x$ for all $x \in \mathbb{R}$. Then the value of $8g'(2)$ is
questions.solution:
$g(f(x)) = x \Rightarrow g'(f(x)) f'(x) = 1 \Rightarrow g'(f(x)) = \frac{1}{f'(x)}$
$f'(x) = 5x^4 + \frac{1}{2} e^{x/4}$
For $f(x) = 2 \Rightarrow x = 0$
$f'(0) = \frac{1}{2}$
$g'(2) = \frac{1}{f'(0)} = 2 \Rightarrow 8g'(2) = 16$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $f(x) = \frac{2x^2 - 3x + 9}{2x^2 + 3x + 4}$. If maximum value of $f(x)$ is $m$ and minimum value of $f(x)$ is $n$ then find $m + n$?
questions.solution:
Let $y = \frac{2x^2 - 3x + 9}{2x^2 + 3x + 4} \Rightarrow y(2x^2 + 3x + 4) = 2x^2 - 3x + 9$
$(y-1)2x^2 + 3x(y+1) + 4y - 9 = 0$
For real $x, D \ge 0 \Rightarrow 9(y+1)^2 - 4(2)(y-1)(4y-9) \ge 0$
$-7y^2 + 70y - 27 \ge 0 \Rightarrow 7y^2 - 70y + 27 \le 0$
Roots $\alpha, \beta = \frac{70 \pm \sqrt{4144}}{14}$
$m + n = \alpha + \beta = \frac{70}{7} = 10$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: $f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{1-\cos 2x}{x^2} & x < 0 \\ \alpha & x = 0 \\ \beta \frac{\sqrt{1-\cos x}}{x} & x > 0 \end{cases}$. If $f(x)$ is continuous at $x = 0$ find $\alpha^2 + \beta^2$.
questions.solution:
$\lim_{x \to 0^-} \frac{1-\cos 2x}{x^2} = 2 = \alpha$
$\lim_{x \to 0^+} \beta \frac{\sqrt{1-\cos x}}{x} = \beta \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 2 \Rightarrow \beta = 2\sqrt{2}$
$\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = 4 + 8 = 12$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the sum and the product of all the nonzero solutions of the equation $(\bar{z})^2 + |z| = 0, z \in \mathbb{C}$ then $4(\alpha^2 + \beta^2)$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$z^2 + |z| = 0 \Rightarrow x^2 - y^2 - 2xyi + \sqrt{x^2+y^2} = 0$
If $y = 0 \Rightarrow x^2 + |x| = 0 \Rightarrow x = 0$
If $x = 0 \Rightarrow -y^2 + |y| = 0 \Rightarrow y = 1, -1$
Solutions: $i, -i$
Sum $\alpha = 0$, Product $\beta = 1$
$4(\alpha^2 + \beta^2) = 4(0 + 1) = 4$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If differential equation satisfies $\frac{dy}{dx} - y = \cos x$ at $x = 0, y = -\frac{1}{2}$. Find $y\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$.
questions.solution:
I.F. $= e^{\int -1 \, dx} = e^{-x}$
$y \cdot e^{-x} = \int e^{-x} \cos x \, dx = \frac{e^{-x} (\sin x - \cos x)}{2} + c$
$y = \frac{\sin x - \cos x}{2} + c e^x$
At $x = 0, y = -1/2 \Rightarrow -1/2 = -1/2 + c \Rightarrow c = 0$
$y = \frac{\sin x - \cos x}{2} \Rightarrow y\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) = 0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{R}$. Let the mean and the variance of 6 observations $-3, 4, 7, -6, \alpha, \beta$ be 2 and 23 respectively. The mean deviation about the mean of these 6 observations is
questions.solution:
$\bar{x} = \frac{-3+4+7-6+\alpha+\beta}{6} = 2 \Rightarrow \alpha + \beta = 10$
$\sigma^2 = 23 = \frac{(-3-2)^2 + (4-2)^2 + (7-2)^2 + (-6-2)^2 + (\alpha-2)^2 + (\beta-2)^2}{6} \Rightarrow \alpha^2 + \beta^2 = 52$
$\Rightarrow \alpha = 6, \beta = 4$
Observations are $-3, 4, 7, -6, 6, 4$.
Mean deviation about mean $= \frac{|-3-2| + |4-2| + |7-2| + |-6-2| + |6-2| + |4-2|}{6} = \frac{5+2+5+8+4+2}{6} = \frac{26}{6} = \frac{13}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the length of focal chord of $y^2 = 12x$ is 15 and if the distance of the focal chord from origin is $p$ then $10p^2$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$y^2 = 4(3)x \Rightarrow a = 3$, focus $= (3, 0)$
Length of focal chord $= a\left(t - t_2\right)^2 = 3\left(t + \frac{1}{t}\right)^2 = 15 \Rightarrow t + \frac{1}{t} = \sqrt{5}$
$t - \frac{1}{t} = 1$
Slope of focal chord $m_{AB} = \frac{2}{t - \frac{1}{t}} = 2$
Equation of chord: $y - 0 = 2(x-3) \Rightarrow 2x - y - 6 = 0$
$p = \frac{|2(0) - 0 - 6|}{\sqrt{2^2 + 1}} = \frac{6}{\sqrt{5}}$
$10p^2 = 10 \times \frac{36}{5} = 72$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Shortest distance between lines $\frac{x+1}{-2} = \frac{y}{2} = \frac{z-1}{1}$ and $\frac{x-5}{2} = \frac{y-2}{-3} = \frac{z-1}{1}$ is $\frac{38k}{6\sqrt{5}}$, find $\int_0^k [x^2] \, dx$
questions.solution:
S.D. $= \frac{|(6\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}) \cdot (5\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 2\hat{k})|}{\sqrt{45}} = \frac{38}{3\sqrt{5}} = \frac{38k}{6\sqrt{5}} \Rightarrow k = 2$
$\int_0^2 [x^2] \, dx = \int_0^1 0 \, dx + \int_1^{\sqrt{2}} 1 \, dx + \int_{\sqrt{2}}^{\sqrt{3}} 2 \, dx + \int_{\sqrt{3}}^2 3 \, dx = (\sqrt{2}-1) + 2(\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2}) + 3(2-\sqrt{3}) = 5 - \sqrt{2} - \sqrt{3}$

questions.text: $y = y(x)$ is a solution of the differential equation $(x^4 + 2x^3 + 3x^2 + 2x + 2) dy - (2x^2 + 2x + 3) dx = 0$. If $y(0) = \frac{\pi}{4}$. Find $y(-1)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Curve $y = 1 + 3x - 2x^2$ and $y = \frac{1}{x}$ intersects at point $\left(\frac{1}{2}, 2\right)$ then area enclosed between curve is $\frac{1}{24}(\sqrt{5}+m) - n \log_e(1+\sqrt{5})$ then find the value of $\ell + m + n$ is
questions.solution:
$1 + 3x - 2x^2 = \frac{1}{x} \Rightarrow 2x^3 - 3x^2 - x + 1 = 0 \Rightarrow x = \frac{1}{2}$ or $x^2 - x - 1 = 0 \Rightarrow x = \frac{1 \pm \sqrt{5}}{2}$
$\text{Area} = \int_{1/2}^{\frac{\sqrt{5}+1}{2}} \left( (-2x^2 + 3x + 1) - \frac{1}{x} \right) dx$
$= \frac{1}{24}[15 + 14\sqrt{5}] - \ln(\sqrt{5}+1)$
Here $\ell = 14, m = 15, n = 1 \Rightarrow \ell + m + n = 14 + 15 + 1 = 30$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A metallic wire of uniform mass density having mass M and length l is bent to form a semicircle. A point mass m is kept at the centre of the semicircle. Find the gravitational forced experienced by m.
questions.solution:
$r = \frac{L}{\pi}$
$dg = \frac{G dm}{r^2} \sin\theta = \frac{G}{r^2} \frac{M}{L} r d\theta \sin\theta$
$g = \int_{0}^{\pi} \frac{G M}{r L} \sin\theta \, d\theta = \frac{GM}{rL}(2)$
$F = mg = \frac{2GMm}{rL} = \frac{2\pi GMm}{L^2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: 5 convex lens are kept together each having power of 25 D. Find the focal length.
questions.solution:
$P_{\text{eq}} = P \times 5 = 25 \times 5 = 125\text{ D}$
$f_{\text{eq}} = \frac{1}{125} \text{ m} = \frac{100}{125} \text{ cm} = 0.8 \text{ cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A body moving with constant acceleration covers 102.5 m in $n^{\text{th}}$ second of its motion and covers 115.0 m in $(n + 2)^{\text{th}}$ second then find its acceleration.
questions.solution:
$S_{n^{\text{th}}} = u + \frac{a}{2}[2n-1] = 102.5$
$S_{(n+2)^{\text{th}}} = u + \frac{a}{2}[2n+3] = 115$
Subtracting: $\frac{a}{2}[4] = 12.5 \Rightarrow 2a = 12.5 \Rightarrow a = 6.25 \text{ m/s}^2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A particle of mass m dropped from height h above the ground. After collision, rises to height h/2. Then loss in energy during collision and speed of particle just before collision respectively are.
questions.solution:
$\Delta E = mg\frac{h}{2} - mgh = -mg\frac{h}{2}$ i.e. 50% loss in energy.
Speed just before collision $v = \sqrt{2gh}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: If the electric field vector at a point in an electromagnetic wave is given by $\vec{E} = 40\cos\left(\omega\left(t - \frac{z}{c}\right)\right) \hat{i}$ then corresponding $\vec{B}$ will be:
questions.solution:
$|B| = \frac{|E|}{c} = \frac{40}{c}\cos\left(\omega\left(t - \frac{z}{c}\right)\right)$
Direction of wave propagation is $+\hat{k}$. Since $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$ is along propagation, $\hat{i} \times \hat{j} = \hat{k}$, so $\vec{B}$ is along $\hat{j}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Infinite charge sheet in xy plane of surface charge density $\sigma$ and infinite long wire of linear charge density $\lambda$ placed at (0, 0, 4) and $\sigma = 2\lambda$. Then net electric field (0, 0, 2).
questions.solution: $E_{\text{net}} = \frac{\sigma}{2\epsilon_0} - \frac{2K\lambda}{r} = \frac{2\lambda}{2\epsilon_0} - \frac{2\lambda}{4\pi\epsilon_0 r} = \frac{\lambda}{\epsilon_0} \left[\frac{2\pi r - 1}{2\pi r}\right]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A hollow cylinder and solid sphere of same mass and radius are rolling with same initial velocity v on a rough inclined plane. Find the ratios of their kinetic energies and maximum height reached by them.
questions.solution:
$K_{\text{cylinder}} = MV^2$
$K_{\text{sphere}} = \frac{7}{10} MV^2$
$\frac{K_{\text{cylinder}}}{K_{\text{sphere}}} = \frac{10}{7}$
Ratio of maximum height is also $\frac{10}{7}$.

questions.text: In given equation $y = 2A \sin\left(\frac{2\pi n t}{\lambda}\right) \cos\left(\frac{2\pi x}{\lambda}\right)$. Find the dimension of n.
questions.solution: $\left[ \frac{2\pi n t}{\lambda} \right] = M^0 L^0 T^0 \Rightarrow [n] = \frac{[\lambda]}{[t]} = [L^1 T^{-1}]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: When a conducting platinum wire is placed in ice, its resistance is $8\Omega$ and when placed in steam it is $10\Omega$. Find the resistance of wire at 400°C.
questions.solution:
$R_T = R_0(1 + \alpha \Delta T)$
$10 = 8(1 + \alpha(100)) \Rightarrow \alpha = \frac{1}{400}$
$R_{400} = 8\left(1 + \frac{1}{400} \times 400\right) = 8(1+1) = 16\Omega$ (Wait, in PDF: $R = 8\left(1 + \frac{1}{400} \times 40\right) = 8.8\Omega$).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Fractional error in image distance and object distance are $\frac{\Delta v}{v}$ and $\frac{\Delta u}{u}$ then find the fractional error in focal length of the given spherical mirror.
questions.solution:
$\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} \Rightarrow f = \frac{uv}{u+v}$
$\frac{df}{f^2} = \frac{dv}{v^2} + \frac{du}{u^2} \Rightarrow \frac{df}{f} = f \left[\frac{dv}{v^2} + \frac{du}{u^2}\right] = \frac{uv}{u+v} \left[\frac{dv}{v^2} + \frac{du}{u^2}\right]$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Instantaneous current in a circuit is zero. In which of the options voltage will be maximum.
(a) L (b) C (c) R (d) LC
questions.solution: Phase difference between current and voltage is $90^\circ$. So possible circuits are (A), (B) and (D).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
x and y coordinates of a body performing some motion is given as:
$x = 3 + 4t$
$y = 3t^2 + 4t$
Identify the trajectory of motion.
questions.solution:
$t = \frac{x-3}{4}$
$y = 3\left(\frac{x-3}{4}\right)^2 + 4\left(\frac{x-3}{4}\right) = \frac{1}{16}(3x^2 - 2x - 21)$
Since $y$ is quadratic in $x$, trajectory is parabola.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Choose the correct graph for kinetic energy vs r for an electron revolving around an infinite line of charge.
questions.solution: $\frac{mv^2}{r} = e \times \frac{2k\lambda}{r} \Rightarrow mv^2 = 2k\lambda e \Rightarrow KE = k\lambda e$, which is constant with respect to r.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Pressure vs temperature graph is given for gas of different density. Compare $\rho_1, \rho_2$ and $\rho_3$?
questions.solution:
$PM = \rho RT \Rightarrow \rho = \frac{PM}{RT} \propto \frac{P}{T} = \text{slope}$
Since $\text{slope}_1 > \text{slope}_2 > \text{slope}_3$, $\rho_1 > \rho_2 > \rho_3$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Work done to expand the bubble of diameter 7 cm and surface tension 40 dyne/cm is 36960 erg. Find the radius of the expanded bubble?
questions.solution:
$\Delta S = \frac{36960}{40 \times 2} = 462\text{ cm}^2$
$4\pi r_f^2 = 462 + 4\pi \left(\frac{7}{2}\right)^2 \Rightarrow r_f^2 = 49 \Rightarrow r_f = 7\text{ cm}$
Diameter $= 14\text{ cm}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: De-Broglie wavelength of electron moving from n = 4 to n = 3 of a hydrogen is $b(\pi a_0)$; Where $a_0$ is bohr radius of the hydrogen atom. Find the value of b.
questions.solution:
$\lambda = \frac{2\pi r}{n} = \frac{2\pi a_0 n^2}{n} = 2\pi a_0 n$
$\lambda_1 = 8\pi a_0, \lambda_2 = 6\pi a_0$
$\Delta\lambda = 2\pi a_0 \Rightarrow b = 2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An elastic string under tension of 3N has a length of ‘a’. If length is ‘b’ then tension is 2N. Find tension when length is (3a – 2b).
questions.solution:
$3F = Ka \Rightarrow a = \frac{3F}{K}$
$2F = Kb \Rightarrow b = \frac{2F}{K}$
$3a - 2b = \frac{9F}{K} - \frac{4F}{K} = \frac{5F}{K}$
